title: Crüger to Müller, 1 July 1622
author: Peter Crüger
summary: Crüger finds Kepler's physical astronomy pleasing but obscure, accuses him of bending Tycho's observations to fit his harmonies and Copernicanism, and turns hopefully to Longomontanus's newly published *Astronomia Danica*.

notes.note: The corrections added to or taken from a planet's mean motion to give its true place. Kepler found them from areas swept out, by what is now his second law.
Kepler's name for a planet's swinging nearer to and farther from the sun, which he compared with the arms of a balance (*Epitome*, book IV).

notes.on: the book on the more recent phenomena of the world
notes.note: Tycho's *De mundi aetherei recentioribus phaenomenis* (1588), on the comet of 1577.
